decision.rationale: At the pre-registered n=3000 stratified sample, the physically relevant noise grid (sigma in {1e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2} p.u.) produced essentially step-invariant rho-margin distributions across all three candidate steps, while finer grids primarily reduced the discretisation floor and modestly increased margin saturation at each step's own discretisation sigma (61.4% > 10 nat at 0.1, 62.6% at 0.05, 65.7% at 0.025). The mu(L) curve also contains genuine regulator-tap discontinuities (63 circuit-wide boundaries, jumps up to 1.4e-2 p.u. -- tap_discontinuities.json), making the original 1e-3 p.u. interpolation criterion unattainable by grid refinement and inappropriate as the selection criterion. Step 0.05 therefore provides an intermediate numerical floor (5.145e-3 p.u. discretisation sigma) without the additional saturation of 0.025, at no additional cost (table already built, 70,142 solves, 0 non-converged, 0 NaN).
decision.not_selected_on: interpolation fidelity alone (see tap_discontinuities.json for why that criterion is unreachable here)
